faq.q: What does the Introduction to Forensic Investigations for Water Losses course cover?
faq.a: This course equips restoration professionals with a systematic forensic methodology, evidence-gathering techniques, failure analysis skills, the ability to present findings professionally, and an understanding of how to establish the financial cost of a loss.; Topics covered: the circumstances that trigger forensic investigations, forensic investigation methods, failure analysis of building systems and materials, presenting findings to insurers and legal representatives, and establishing the total cost of loss.; Standards applied: IICRC S500, relevant Australian Standard AS 4349 series (inspection of buildings), state civil procedure rules for expert evidence.

faq.q: What is the focus of the Introduction to Forensic Investigations for Water Losses course?
faq.a: Forensic water damage investigations are conducted to answer specific factual questions about a water loss: what caused it, when it started, how far it spread, and whether the remediation was adequate.
